To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a model can be developed for selecting the sites for microscopic evaluation of tissue blocks from arteries and that the probability of obtaining the required tissue characteristics increases with the number of sites selected.

the probability of obtaining the tissue characteristic desired by an investigator is higher when purposive selection is employed than when a random selection is used, but the difference between purposive and random selection decreases as the number of tissue sites sampled increases.

purposive selection of tissue sites for microscopic examination of atherosclerosis in the thoracic aorta of the baboon increases the probability of obtaining the required tissue characteristics in the low number of tissue sites selected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a probability model to aid investigators in choosing the location of sites for obtaining tissue blocks from arteries and the number of such sites to be obtained.
the development and evaluation of an optimal selection of sites for microscopic examination of arterial tissue blocks in the presence of gross arterial lesions.
the selection of sites for microscopic examination of arteries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the probability of obtaining a desired number of tissue blocks from a gross lesion in a random sample of n sites from a gross arterial specimen is less than that of purposive selection of n sites.

, when the investigator is concerned about the probability of obtaining tissue blocks for microscopic study, the number of sites should be increased to a level that is sufficient for the desired probability level.

, if the investigator is interested only in the probability of obtaining a block from the lesion and does not care whether the probability of obtaining the block from an area of no lesion is also known, then the purposive situation would be the best.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
purposive sampling should not be used for the selection of sites for microscopic evaluation of arteries.

, for most practical purposes, the investigator can select a few purposive sites to increase the probability of obtaining the tissue blocks of interest and still maintain the statistical inference of a random selection.

the investigator should select a site purposively if the investigator is interested only in the gross lesion and if the investigator is concerned about the cost and the time involved in obtaining a tissue sample from a gross lesion.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the probability model can be used to help an investigator choose the number and location of tissue samples to be taken from a gross arterial specimen to optimize the probability of obtaining the tissue characteristics desired for microscopic evaluation.

the probability of obtaining the tissue characteristics of interest in the purposive selection of sites is greater than in random selection when a small number of sites is selected and the increase in the probability of obtaining a tissue block for microscopic examination from the lesion and from an area free from lesions is less than that of the increase in the number of sites in the random selection of sites.
purposive selection of sites is more efficient than random selection when the investigator is interested only in the presence of gross and microscopic lesions.
